While much of the focus over the last few years on social media has been on Facebook and Instagram, LinkedIn has been steadily growing its user base to more than [500 million users](https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/the-rise-of-the-new-linkedin-by-the-numbers-infographic/508519/).
And we’ve seen first-hand that businesses are working hard on [perfecting their LinkedIn marketing strategy](https://buffer.com/resources/the-silent-rise-of-linkedin/) so that they can tap into the world’s largest professional network.
A few months ago, we asked you (our readers) to let us know which social media networks you would like to learn more about – LinkedIn (53%) came in a close second, just after Instagram (62%).
To get started, we teamed up with LinkedIn to share with you tried and true tips on how to leverage one of the most valuable online resources for your business: your LinkedIn Company Page.
With this simple 5-step strategy your business can accelerate the growth of your Company Page by up to 600 percent.
Let’s get started!
5 LinkedIn marketing tips to grow your Company Page 600% faster
LinkedIn is only just getting started!
CEO Jeff Weiner [plans to](https://ourstory.linkedin.com/) “develop the world’s first economic graph” with the hopes of “digitally mapping out the global economy.” A goal not far from reach seeing how LinkedIn has an in-depth dataset of company, industry, and individual contact information for more than 500 million members.
In the long-term, [LinkedIn marketing](https://buffer.com/resources/the-silent-rise-of-linkedin/) will be a game-changer for businesses and brands in the B2B space. Here are 5 tips to put your business of the forefront of this trend.

### 1. Complete your LinkedIn company profile (fully)
Did you know that Company Pages with complete profiles receive up to 2X more visitors than those with incomplete page profiles?
Make sure your page has the following seven items completely filled out:
– Logo
– Company description
– Website URL
– Company size
– Industry
– Company type
– Location
In order to fully complete your profile, head to your Company Page on LinkedIn and select “Overview”:
From there, you’ll be directed to your company’s information page where you can update all of the most important details about your business, including:
Make sure to upload a high-resolution company logo and a cover image that captures your brand as well as fill out the “About us” section to provide visitors with more information.
Below the “About us” section you’ll find even more important fields to complete:
Having a complete company profile (website URL, company size, industry, type, and location) are all important components in helping to make your Company Page look more legitimate and professional.
Legitimacy and professionalism are critical for brand image, and provides visitors with all the information they need to connect with your company when they’re ready.

### 2. Create a consistent posting schedule
According to LinkedIn, businesses that post at least once per month have been shown to gain followers 6X faster than those that don’t.
In addition, Company Pages with at least 150 followers typically get 5X more Company Page views than those with fewer followers!
You should aim to post at least once per week to your Company Page to keep your followers engaged (we post twice per week). To help you post consistently to your Company Page, [set up a posting schedule](https://buffer.com/) so that you can easily schedule posts for your Page:
We’ve found that our LinkedIn content performs really well if we include the following:

- Descriptive caption: Helps to provide people with extra context around your content
- Eye-catching images: Clean, simple aesthetic helps your content to stand out
- Hashtags: A great way to increase the visibility of your content to new audiences
- Bonus: Add emojis, questions, and bullet points to switch up the look and feel of your content
If you’re unsure what to post to LinkedIn, or if you’d like a steady stream of quality content, we suggest taking some time to [add a few RSS feeds](https://faq.buffer.com/article/303-publish-content-inbox) to your content inbox.
(Quick note: RSS feeds are only available in our [paid plans](https://buffer.com/pricing)).
We’ve been using RSS feeds in tandem with our LinkedIn marketing strategy for years and we’ve found that it provides us with a solid supply of content to share all the time. The key with RSS feeds is to [customize the content](https://buffer.com/resources/discover-content-ideas/)  using some of the tips we shared above.
Try to avoid simply posting the headline and image provided with the article in the RSS feed. The same best-practices that you implement when posting your own quality content also apply to [curated content](https://buffer.com/resources/guide-to-content-curation/) shared on LinkedIn.

### 3. Re-Buffer your top content
If you find that your business is running out of content ideas, we recommend to (sparingly) re-share, or Re-Buffer, your top posts from the past. Due to sophisticated [social media algorithms](https://buffer.com/resources/social-media-algorithms-show-notes/), it’s likely that only a [very small](https://buffer.com/resources/3rd-party-social-media-tools/) percentage (2-6%) of your followers have seen your posts in the LinkedIn Feed.
If you have a [backlog of successful social media content](https://buffer.com/resources/save-time-social-media-scheduling/), it’s likely that the content will perform well again in the future.
You can find your top posts under the analytics section on your Buffer dashboard. Select your Posts Report and click “Most Popular”.
(Quick note: The Re-Buffer feature is only available in our [paid plans](https://buffer.com/pricing)).
LinkedIn Pulse – or the LinkedIn Feed – no longer operates as a separate application within LinkedIn. It’s seamlessly integrated into members’ feeds as articles to help enhance the content-first experience.
It’s working, too! More than 100,000 organic articles are published weekly on LinkedIn, many of which are written by top-level executives at brands around the world. However, more content means less space in the News Feed, which means your business needs a rock-solid LinkedIn marketing strategy.
Set yourself up for success by re-sharing your top-performing content on a consistent basis – a crucial piece in growing your Company Page.

### 4. Engage your colleagues and employees
One of the most influential groups of people that can help you with your LinkedIn marketing is your colleagues and employees. When activated, they can boost your Linkedin content while simultaneously increasing the visibility of your Company Page on LinkedIn.
Help them help you! Here’s how to get your colleagues and employees involved:

#### Encourage colleagues to engage with your content
According to LinkedIn, encouraging your colleagues and employees to engage with your posts will help to spread to the content their networks, therefore [increasing your company’s reach](https://buffer.com/resources/social-media-news-episode-106/) on LinkedIn. As it turns out, the people closest to you could be the biggest asset in amplifying your LinkedIn marketing strategy and growth.

We’ve been using RSS feeds in tandem with our LinkedIn marketing strategy for years and we’ve found that it provides us with a solid supply of content to share all the time. The key with RSS feeds is to [customize the content](https://buffer.com/resources/discover-content-ideas/)  using some of the tips we shared above.
Try to avoid simply posting the headline and image provided with the article in the RSS feed. The same best-practices that you implement when posting your own quality content also apply to [curated content](https://buffer.com/resources/guide-to-content-curation/) shared on LinkedIn.

### 3. Re-Buffer your top content
If you find that your business is running out of content ideas, we recommend to (sparingly) re-share, or Re-Buffer, your top posts from the past. Due to sophisticated [social media algorithms](https://buffer.com/resources/social-media-algorithms-show-notes/), it’s likely that only a [very small](https://buffer.com/resources/3rd-party-social-media-tools/) percentage (2-6%) of your followers have seen your posts in the LinkedIn Feed.
If you have a [backlog of successful social media content](https://buffer.com/resources/save-time-social-media-scheduling/), it’s likely that the content will perform well again in the future.
You can find your top posts under the analytics section on your Buffer dashboard. Select your Posts Report and click “Most Popular”.
(Quick note: The Re-Buffer feature is only available in our [paid plans](https://buffer.com/pricing)).
LinkedIn Pulse – or the LinkedIn Feed – no longer operates as a separate application within LinkedIn. It’s seamlessly integrated into members’ feeds as articles to help enhance the content-first experience.
It’s working, too! More than 100,000 organic articles are published weekly on LinkedIn, many of which are written by top-level executives at brands around the world. However, more content means less space in the News Feed, which means your business needs a rock-solid LinkedIn marketing strategy.
Set yourself up for success by re-sharing your top-performing content on a consistent basis – a crucial piece in growing your Company Page.

### 4. Engage your colleagues and employees
One of the most influential groups of people that can help you with your LinkedIn marketing is your colleagues and employees. When activated, they can boost your Linkedin content while simultaneously increasing the visibility of your Company Page on LinkedIn.
Help them help you! Here’s how to get your colleagues and employees involved:

#### Encourage colleagues to engage with your content
According to LinkedIn, encouraging your colleagues and employees to engage with your posts will help to spread to the content their networks, therefore [increasing your company’s reach](https://buffer.com/resources/social-media-news-episode-106/) on LinkedIn. # Z.E Digital Tech - LinkedIn Growth Strategy
## Goal: 10,000 Followers in 3 Weeks

**Current Status:** 2 followers (Feb 28, 2026)
**Target:** 10,000 followers by March 21, 2026
**Required Growth:** ~476 followers/day average

---

## 🎯 Content Themes & Pillars

### Primary Themes (70% of content)
1. **AI Innovation & Trends** - Hottest topic on LinkedIn (284K+ likes category)
   - LLM developments, AGI progress, AI agents
   - Practical AI applications for businesses
   - Behind-the-scenes of our AI projects (ELO-AGI, Sofia Concierge)

2. **Tech Insights & Tutorials** - High engagement, educational
   - Quick tips, code snippets, architecture patterns
   - "How we built X" series
   - Tech stack breakdowns

3. **Digital Transformation** - B2B appeal
   - Case studies with clients
   - ROI of modernizing tech
   - Digital transformation stories

### Secondary Themes (30% of content)
4. **Company Culture & Team** - Human connection
   - Work snapshots, team achievements
   - Office life in Tirana
   - Hiring/remote work culture

5. **Industry Commentary** - Thought leadership
   - Hot takes on tech news
   - Predictions and analysis
   - Weekly tech roundups

---

## 📅 3-Week Content Calendar

### Week 1: Foundation & Visibility (Feb 28 - Mar 6)
**Focus:** Brand awareness, profile optimization, initial engagement

| Day | Post Type | Content Theme | Hashtags |
|-----|-----------|---------------|----------|
| Day 1 | Announcement | Company intro (POSTED) | #WebDevelopment #AI |
| Day 2 | Carousel | "5 AI Tools We Use Daily at Z.E Digital" | #AITools #Productivity |
| Day 3 | Story | Behind Sofia Hotel Concierge project | #AI #Hospitality |
| Day 4 | Poll | "What's your biggest tech challenge in 2026?" | #TechTrends #Business |
| Day 5 | Tutorial | "How to Build a Simple AI Chatbot in 10 Minutes" | #AI #Tutorial |
| Day 6 | Insight | "Why 96.4% AI Accuracy Matters for Your Business" | #AI #Business |
| Day 7 | Weekly Recap | Tech news roundup + our take | #TechNews #Innovation |

### Week 2: Engagement & Authority (Mar 7 - Mar 13)
**Focus:** Thought leadership, community engagement, collaborations

| Day | Post Type | Content Theme | Hashtags |
|-----|-----------|---------------|----------|
| Day 8 | Case Study | "How We Built ELO-AGI: 38 Cognitive Modules Explained" | #AGI #AI |
| Day 9 | Video/Text | "3 Cybersecurity Mistakes Killing Your Business" | #Cybersecurity |
| Day 10 | Carousel | "Web Development in 2026: What's Changed" | #WebDevelopment |
| Day 11 | Story | Client success story (anonymized) | #ClientSuccess |
| Day 12 | Opinion | Hot take on latest AI regulation/news | #AI #Policy |
| Day 13 | Tutorial | "Deploy Your First AI Model - Step by Step" | #AI #Tutorial |
| Day 14 | Weekly Recap | AI/tech news + predictions | #TechNews |

### Week 3: Scale & Virality (Mar 14 - Mar 20)
**Focus:** Viral content, controversial takes, high engagement

| Day | Post Type | Content Theme | Hashtags |
|-----|-----------|---------------|----------|
| Day 15 | Controversy | "Why Most AI Projects Fail (And How to Fix Yours)" | #AI #Startups |
| Day 16 | Data/Stats | Infographic: "State of AI Adoption 2026" | #AI #Data |
| Day 17 | Story | "From Albania to Global: Our Journey" | #StartupStory |
| Day 18 | Carousel | "10 Free Tools to Replace Expensive Software" | #Productivity #Tools |
| Day 19 | Prediction | "What AI Will Look Like in 2027" | #AI #Future |
| Day 20 | Hiring | "We're Looking for Talent" (even if not actively) | #Hiring #Remote |
| Day 21 | Celebration | "3 Weeks, 10K Followers - Thank You!" | #Community |

---

## 🚀 Daily Engagement Routine (30-60 min/day)

### Morning (15 min)
- [ ] Comment on 5 trending posts in #AI #WebDevelopment #Cybersecurity
- [ ] Like and reply to all comments on our posts
- [ ] Share 1 relevant industry article with commentary

### Afternoon (15 min)
- [ ] Engage with 5 potential client accounts (CEOs, CTOs, Founders)
- [ ] Comment thoughtfully on influencer posts in tech space
- [ ] Connect with 10 new relevant people

### Evening (15 min)
- [ ] Respond to all DMs and comments
- [ ] Schedule next day's post
- [ ] Engage with 3 competitor pages (not direct)

---

## 🎯 Target Accounts to Engage With

### Tech Influencers (Comment on their posts daily)
- Sam Altman (OpenAI)
- Yann LeCun (Meta AI)
- Andrew Ng (DeepLearning.AI)
- Andrej Karpathy
- Lex Fridman
- Thomas Bornheim (local - Arkadia Heilbronn)
- 42 Heilbronn (local tech community)

### Tech Companies (Engage, don't compete)
- OpenAI
- Anthropic
- Vercel
- Supabase
- Linear
- Notion

### Local/Regional (High engagement potential)
- Albanian tech community
- Balkan startups
- German tech scene (Heilbronn region)

---

## 📊 Growth Tactics

### 1. Hashtag Strategy
**Use 3-5 hashtags per post:**
- 2 broad: #AI #WebDevelopment #Technology
- 2 niche: #AIAgents #LLM #Cybersecurity
- 1 branded: #ZEDigitalTech (create momentum)

### 2. Post Format Priority
1. **Carousels** - 1.4x more reach
2. **Text + Image** - Good for tutorials
3. **Polls** - High engagement
4. **Videos** - Native video gets promoted
5. **Documents/PDFs** - Carousel alternative

### 3. Optimal Posting Times (Europe timezone)
- **Best:** Tuesday-Thursday, 8-10 AM or 5-6 PM CET
- **Good:** Monday, Wednesday, Friday same times
- **Avoid:** Weekends (unless testing)

### 4. Engagement Hacks
- Ask questions in posts (boosts comments)
- Use "Line breaks" for readability
- First 2 lines = hook (visible before "see more")
- End with CTA: "Agree?", "What's your experience?", "👇"

---

## 🔥 Viral Content Templates

### Template 1: Controversial Take
```
[Hot Take Statement]

Here's why I disagree with the mainstream view:

1. [Point 1]
2. [Point 2]  
3. [Point 3]

[Proof/Example from our work]

Agree or disagree? 👇
```

### Template 2: Behind the Scenes
```
We just shipped [Project].

Here's what nobody tells you about building [type of project]:

✅ What worked:
- [Point]
- [Point]

❌ What didn't:
- [Point]
- [Point]

[Key lesson]

Save this for your next project 📌
```

### Template 3: Data-Driven Insight
```
[Surprising statistic]

After analyzing [X] projects, here's what we found:

📊 [Data point 1]
📊 [Data point 2]
📊 [Data point 3]

The pattern is clear: [Insight]

[CTA]
```

---

## 📈 KPIs to Track

| Metric | Week 1 | Week 2 | Week 3 |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Followers | 500 | 2,500 | 10,000 |
| Post Impressions | 5,000 | 25,000 | 100,000 |
| Engagement Rate | 5%+ | 5%+ | 5%+ |
| Comments/Post | 10+ | 50+ | 100+ |
| Profile Views | 500 | 2,500 | 10,000 |

---

## ⚡ Quick Wins (Do Today)

1. [x] Post company introduction ✅ DONE
2. [ ] Complete profile 100% (add services, specialties)
3. [ ] Follow 50 relevant pages
4. [ ] Connect with 20 local tech people
5. [ ] Comment on 10 trending AI posts
6. [ ] Create Week 1 content in advance
7. [ ] Set up posting reminders

---

## 🎨 Content Bank (Ready-to-Post)

### Post 2: AI Tools Carousel
**Slide 1:** "5 AI Tools We Use Daily at Z.E Digital Tech"
**Slide 2:** Cursor - AI coding assistant (10x productivity)
**Slide 3:** Perplexity - Research at lightning speed
**Slide 4:** Claude/GPT - Content & brainstorming
**Slide 5:** ElevenLabs - Voice cloning for demos
**Slide 6:** Replicate - Quick model deployment
**Slide 7:** What's your favorite AI tool? Comment below 👇

### Post 3: Sofia Concierge Story
**Hook:** "We built an AI that speaks German to hotel guests. Here's how:"
**Body:** 
- Challenge: Hotel Lärchenhof needed 24/7 guest support
- Solution: AI voice assistant via Twilio SIP + LiveKit
- Result: Handles inquiries in natural German conversation
- Tech: Python, Cartesia TTS, Deepgram, OpenRouter
**CTA:** "Want to see it in action? Link in comments 👇"

### Post 4: Poll
**Question:** "What's your biggest tech challenge in 2026?"
**Options:**
- AI integration
- Cybersecurity
- Scaling infrastructure
- Hiring tech talent

---

## 🤝 Engagement Scripts

### For CEO/Founder Posts:
"Great insights, [Name]! We've seen similar patterns with our clients at Z.E Digital Tech. The key is [relevant tip]. Would love to connect!"

### For Tech Tutorial Posts:
"Solid breakdown! 🔥 We use a similar approach but found [variation] works better for [use case]. Thanks for sharing!"

### For Industry News:
"This is exactly why we're betting on [technology]. The implications for [industry] are massive. Great analysis!"

---

                              - text: "A compelling analogy — AI literacy as the new alphabet. Though I'd add one caveat: knowing 12 terms is the starting point, not the destination. It's like knowing letters without being able to read. What truly matters is understanding the interdependencies between these concepts. The interplay between temperature and prompting strategy directly determines whether a RAG pipeline returns a grounded answer or a confident hallucination. Fine-tuning without robust evaluation (BLEU, ROUGE, human feedback) is guesswork at scale. And context windows without tokenisation cost awareness lead to unnecessarily expensive solutions. I'd also suggest this list is missing a few terms essential for any serious implementation conversation: agentic workflows, function calling, guardrails, and evaluation frameworks. These separate a polished demo from a production-grade system. The core thesis is spot on though. The question is no longer \"should we use AI?\" — it's \"how do we architect systems where AI operates as a reliable decision-making component?\" That requires considerably more than a glossary."

                              - text: "A compelling analogy — AI literacy as the new alphabet. Though I'd add one caveat: knowing 12 terms is the starting point, not the destination. It's like knowing letters without being able to read. What truly matters is understanding the interdependencies between these concepts. The interplay between temperature and prompting strategy directly determines whether a RAG pipeline returns a grounded answer or a confident hallucination. Fine-tuning without robust evaluation (BLEU, ROUGE, human feedback) is guesswork at scale. And context windows without tokenisation cost awareness lead to unnecessarily expensive solutions. I'd also suggest this list is missing a few terms essential for any serious implementation conversation: agentic workflows, function calling, guardrails, and evaluation frameworks. These separate a polished demo from a production-grade system. The core thesis is spot on though. The question is no longer \"should we use AI?\" — it's \"how do we architect systems where AI operates as a reliable decision-making component?\" That requires considerably more than a glossary."

                        - text: Some Fridays feel like a glimpse into the future — today was one of them.

                        - text: At lunch, I had a great exchange with our IT Enterprise Architects about AI — not as hype, but as a real structural shift. How will AI reshape TRUMPF in the near future? What does it mean for our architecture, governance, and scalability? These conversations make transformation tangible. 🤖
                        - text: "And as a highlight, we welcomed our first humanoid robot in laser technology. Discussing secure integration into our infrastructure, future compute needs, and the development toolchain made it clear: this is just the beginning. The first colleagues are already in training. 🦾"
                        - text: Thank you for allowing me to take a few steps on my own, the demonstration and your time

                        - text: . 😊 It’s a lot of fun and so impresive what‘s today and hopefully possible in near future!
                        - text: Moments like these show how fast production, product development and IT are growing together. 🤝🏼
                        - text: After a friday like this, the weekend feels well earned — before heading to Warsaw on Sunday. ✈️

                        - text: Some Fridays feel like a glimpse into the future — today was one of them.
                        - text: We kicked off our project for connected tools in production, taking another step toward a truly data-driven Smart Factory. Seeing manufacturing, IT, and connectivity converge like this is always energizing. 🚀
                        - text: At lunch, I had a great exchange with our IT Enterprise Architects about AI — not as hype, but as a real structural shift. How will AI reshape TRUMPF in the near future? What does it mean for our architecture, governance, and scalability? These conversations make transformation tangible. 🤖
                        - text: "And as a highlight, we welcomed our first humanoid robot in laser technology. Discussing secure integration into our infrastructure, future compute needs, and the development toolchain made it clear: this is just the beginning. The first colleagues are already in training. 🦾"

                    - paragraph [ref=e1841]:
                        - text: Today, I saw a colleague frustrated at the office.
                        - text: He was working on an Expense Tracker assignment as part of his internship at
                        - link "Dream Code Ltd" [ref=e1843] [cursor=pointer]:
                          - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/dream-code-ltd/
                          - strong [ref=e1845]: Dream Code Ltd
                        - text: and he relied heavily on GitHub Copilot to generate most of the code. Unfortunately, his monthly limit was reached -- and suddenly, he felt stuck. No clear direction. No control. Just frustration.
                        - text: That moment said a lot.
                        - text: AI coding agents are powerful. They save time. They autocomplete logic. They even "think" ahead. But when they start building everything for you, something changes -- you stop following the logic deeply. You stop owning the structure. And when something breaks, you feel lost.
                        - text: "You find yourself saying:"
                        - text: "\"That's not what I wanted.\""
                        - text: "\"Why did it delete that function?\""
                        - text: "\"This isn't how I planned it.\""
                        - text: The problem isn't AI.
                        - text: The problem is losing control of your own thinking process.
                        - text: If you use tools like ChatGPT or DeepSeek in a guided way -- asking for explanations, breaking down logic, reviewing snippets before pasting -- you stay involved. You understand what's happening. You remain the engineer.
                        - text: AI should assist your reasoning, not replace it.
                        - text: "To fellow programmers: Use AI as a tool, not as a crutch. Stay in control of your architecture. Read every line you paste. Understand every function you run."
                        - text: Because at the end of the day, when the agent hits its limit...
                        - text: Your knowledge shouldn't.
                        - text: Any comments on AI Agents, software engineers? Feel free in the comments, let's interact

                    - paragraph [ref=e1841]:
                        - text: Today, I saw a colleague frustrated at the office.
                        - text: He was working on an Expense Tracker assignment as part of his internship at
                        - link "Dream Code Ltd" [ref=e1843] [cursor=pointer]:
                          - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/dream-code-ltd/
                          - strong [ref=e1845]: Dream Code Ltd
                        - text: and he relied heavily on GitHub Copilot to generate most of the code. Unfortunately, his monthly limit was reached -- and suddenly, he felt stuck. No clear direction. No control. Just frustration.
                        - text: That moment said a lot.
                        - text: AI coding agents are powerful. They save time. They autocomplete logic. They even "think" ahead. But when they start building everything for you, something changes -- you stop following the logic deeply. You stop owning the structure. And when something breaks, you feel lost.
                        - text: "You find yourself saying:"
                        - text: "\"That's not what I wanted.\""
                        - text: "\"Why did it delete that function?\""
                        - text: "\"This isn't how I planned it.\""
                        - text: The problem isn't AI.
                        - text: The problem is losing control of your own thinking process.
                        - text: If you use tools like ChatGPT or DeepSeek in a guided way -- asking for explanations, breaking down logic, reviewing snippets before pasting -- you stay involved. You understand what's happening. You remain the engineer.
                        - text: AI should assist your reasoning, not replace it.
                        - text: "To fellow programmers: Use AI as a tool, not as a crutch. Stay in control of your architecture. Read every line you paste. Understand every function you run."
                        - text: Because at the end of the day, when the agent hits its limit...
                        - text: Your knowledge shouldn't.

                        - text: Today, I saw a colleague frustrated at the office.
                        - text: He was working on an Expense Tracker assignment as part of his internship at
                        - link "Dream Code Ltd" [ref=e1843] [cursor=pointer]:
                          - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/dream-code-ltd/
                          - strong [ref=e1845]: Dream Code Ltd
                        - text: and he relied heavily on GitHub Copilot to generate most of the code. Unfortunately, his monthly limit was reached -- and suddenly, he felt stuck. No clear direction. No control. Just frustration.
                        - text: That moment said a lot.
                        - text: AI coding agents are powerful. They save time. They autocomplete logic. They even "think" ahead. But when they start building everything for you, something changes -- you stop following the logic deeply. You stop owning the structure. And when something breaks, you feel lost.
                        - text: "You find yourself saying:"
                        - text: "\"That's not what I wanted.\""
                        - text: "\"Why did it delete that function?\""
                        - text: "\"This isn't how I planned it.\""
                        - text: The problem isn't AI.
                        - text: The problem is losing control of your own thinking process.
                        - text: If you use tools like ChatGPT or DeepSeek in a guided way -- asking for explanations, breaking down logic, reviewing snippets before pasting -- you stay involved. You understand what's happening. You remain the engineer.
                        - text: AI should assist your reasoning, not replace it.
                        - text: "To fellow programmers: Use AI as a tool, not as a crutch. Stay in control of your architecture. Read every line you paste. Understand every function you run."
                        - text: Because at the end of the day, when the agent hits its limit...
                        - text: Your knowledge shouldn't.

                    - paragraph [ref=e1841]:
                        - text: Today, I saw a colleague frustrated at the office.
                        - text: He was working on an Expense Tracker assignment as part of his internship at
                        - link "Dream Code Ltd" [ref=e1843] [cursor=pointer]:
                          - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/dream-code-ltd/
                          - strong [ref=e1845]: Dream Code Ltd
                        - text: and he relied heavily on GitHub Copilot to generate most of the code. Unfortunately, his monthly limit was reached -- and suddenly, he felt stuck. No clear direction. No control. Just frustration.
                        - text: That moment said a lot.
                        - text: AI coding agents are powerful. They save time. They autocomplete logic. They even "think" ahead. But when they start building everything for you, something changes -- you stop following the logic deeply. You stop owning the structure. And when something breaks, you feel lost.
                        - text: "You find yourself saying:"
                        - text: "\"That's not what I wanted.\""
                        - text: "\"Why did it delete that function?\""
                        - text: "\"This isn't how I planned it.\""
                        - text: The problem isn't AI.
                        - text: The problem is losing control of your own thinking process.
                        - text: If you use tools like ChatGPT or DeepSeek in a guided way -- asking for explanations, breaking down logic, reviewing snippets before pasting -- you stay involved. You understand what's happening. You remain the engineer.
                        - text: AI should assist your reasoning, not replace it.
                        - text: "To fellow programmers: Use AI as a tool, not as a crutch. Stay in control of your architecture. Read every line you paste. Understand every function you run."
                        - text: Because at the end of the day, when the agent hits its limit...
                        - text: Your knowledge shouldn't.
                        - text: Any comments on AI Agents, software engineers? Feel free in the comments, let's interact

arguments.content:
# Z.E Digital Tech LinkedIn Growth Plan

**Goal:** Grow company page from 2 → 500+ followers in 6 months

## Daily Routine (30-45 min total)

### Morning Block (15 min) - 8:00-9:00 AM
- [ ] **Engage with 5 AI/tech posts** - meaningful comments (not just "Great!")
- [ ] **React to 10 posts** in feed (like, celebrate, insightful)
- [ ] **Check notifications** - respond to any comments on your posts

### Afternoon Block (15 min) - 2:00-3:00 PM
- [ ] **Engage with 5 hospitality/tech posts** - target Sofia's audience
- [ ] **Send 3-5 connection requests** to:
  - Hotel GMs, CTOs, Innovation Managers
  - AI/ML professionals in DACH region
  - Tech journalists and influencers
- [ ] **Comment on 1 trending industry post**

### Evening Block (10 min) - 6:00-7:00 PM
- [ ] **Engage with 3 posts** from connections
- [ ] **Review analytics** - which comments got engagement?
- [ ] **Save promising posts** for future content ideas

---

## Weekly Content Calendar

| Day | Content Type | Topic Focus |
|-----|--------------|-------------|
| **Monday** | Industry Insight | AI trends in hospitality/enterprise |
| **Tuesday** | Company Update | Project wins, team news, Sofia updates |
| **Wednesday** | Thought Leadership | Opinion piece on tech/business |
| **Thursday** | Case Study/Story | Client success, problem-solving |
| **Friday** | Light/Fun | Team culture, behind-the-scenes, weekend vibes |

### Post Templates

**Monday - Industry Insight:**
```
📊 [Trend/Stat]

[Your take - 2-3 sentences]

[Question to spark engagement]

#AI #HospitalityTech #DigitalTransformation
```

**Tuesday - Company Update:**
```
🚀 [What happened]

[Impact/meaning - 2 sentences]

[Tag relevant people/companies]

#ZEDigitalTech #Innovation
```

**Wednesday - Thought Leadership:**
```
[Controversial/provocative statement]

[Your reasoning - 3-4 sentences]

[Call to action or question]

#Leadership #TechTrends
```

**Thursday - Case Study:**
```
🎯 Challenge: [Client's problem]

💡 Our approach: [What you did]

📈 Result: [Measurable outcome]

[Tag client if allowed]

#CaseStudy #AIImplementation
```

**Friday - Culture/Fun:**
```
[Behind-the-scenes moment]

[Personal touch]

[Engagement question]

#CompanyCulture #FridayFeeling
```

---

## Target Hashtags (rotate 3-5 per post)

**Primary:**
- #AI #ArtificialIntelligence #MachineLearning
- #HospitalityTech #HotelTech
- #DigitalTransformation

**Secondary:**
- #Innovation #TechTrends #FutureOfWork
- #VoiceAI #ConversationalAI
- #DACH #GermanTech #BerlinTech

**Niche:**
- #SmartHotel #HotelInnovation
- #EnterpriseAI #AISolutions

---

## Target Accounts to Engage With

### AI/Tech Influencers
- @genaiworks
- @trumpf
- @nvidia
- @googlecloud
- @microsoft
- @openai

### Hospitality Tech
- @mews
- @cloudbeds
- @oraclehospitality
- @hortonworks
- Hotel management publications

### Local/German
- @germanstartups
- @berlinvalley
- @bitcombund
- German tech journalists

---

## Connection Strategy

### Target Profiles (send 3-5 requests daily)
1. **Hotel Decision Makers**
   - General Managers
   - CTOs/Directors of IT
   - Innovation Managers
   - Operations Directors

2. **Tech Ecosystem**
   - AI/ML Engineers
   - Product Managers
   - Tech Founders (DACH)
   - Venture Capitalists

3. **Media/Influencers**
   - Tech journalists
   - Industry analysts
   - Conference speakers

### Connection Request Template:
```
Hi [Name], I noticed your work in [their field]. 
We're building AI solutions for hospitality at Z.E Digital Tech. 
Would love to connect and share insights!
```

---

## Monthly Milestones

| Month | Followers | Posts | Comments | Connections |
|-------|-----------|-------|----------|-------------|
| 1 | 50 | 16 | 120+ | 100 |
| 2 | 100 | 16 | 240+ | 200 |
| 3 | 175 | 16 | 360+ | 350 |
| 4 | 275 | 16 | 480+ | 500 |
| 5 | 375 | 16 | 600+ | 700 |
| 6 | 500+ | 16 | 720+ | 900+ |

---

## Key Metrics to Track

1. **Follower Growth** - Weekly
2. **Post Impressions** - Per post
3. **Engagement Rate** - (Likes+Comments+Shares)/Impressions
4. **Comment Reach** - Impressions from comments
5. **Connection Acceptance Rate** - % of requests accepted
6. **Profile Views** - Weekly trend

---

## Tools & Automation

- **Cron reminders** - 3x daily engagement prompts
- **Weekly analytics review** - Every Sunday
- **Content batching** - Write posts on Sunday for the week
- **Hashtag rotation** - Track which perform best

---

## Do's and Don'ts

### ✅ Do:
- Be authentic and add value
- Respond to all comments within 24h
- Tag people/companies when relevant
- Use native video (higher reach)
- Cross-post employee content
- Celebrate wins publicly

### ❌ Don't:
- Post without engagement strategy
- Use clickbait or misleading headlines
- Ignore negative comments (address professionally)
- Over-post (quality > quantity)
- Be overly promotional
- Copy-paste the same comment

---

## Crisis/Opportunity Protocol

**Viral Post (>1000 impressions):**
1. Respond to ALL comments
2. Share to personal profile
3. Create follow-up post within 48h
4. Reach out to engaged users

**Negative Feedback:**
1. Acknowledge within 2h
2. Take to DM if complex
3. Learn and adapt
4. Don't delete (unless abusive)

---

*Last updated: 2026-02-28*
*Next review: 2026-03-07*

                      - text: What happens when building becomes easier than being used?
                      - text: We’re witnessing something unprecedented. Millions of AI-generated apps are being created in months. Yet only a fraction ever reaches production. Fewer still gain sustained users.
                      - text: The barrier to coding has collapsed. Distribution, adoption, and retention remain unchanged.
                      - text: "This is the uncomfortable shift: we haven’t built a SaaS explosion. We’ve built a prototyping explosion."
                      - text: When anyone can launch in hours, supply skyrockets. But demand still follows trust, relevance, and clear value. The median AI-built app doesn’t fail because of poor code. It fails because no one knows it exists or why it matters.
                      - text: From my perspective, this is a strategic wake-up call.
                      - text: The competitive edge is no longer technical capability alone. It’s positioning, problem clarity, user insight, and go-to-market discipline.
                      - text: AI has democratised creation. It has not democratised distribution.
                      - text: The builders who win won’t just ship faster. They’ll think harder about who they’re serving and why their solution deserves attention.
                      - text: "So here’s the real question:"
                      - text: Are you optimising for building… or for being chosen?

                      - text: What happens when building becomes easier than being used?
                      - text: We’re witnessing something unprecedented. Millions of AI-generated apps are being created in months. Yet only a fraction ever reaches production. Fewer still gain sustained users.
                      - text: The barrier to coding has collapsed. Distribution, adoption, and retention remain unchanged.
                      - text: "This is the uncomfortable shift: we haven’t built a SaaS explosion. We’ve built a prototyping explosion."
                      - text: When anyone can launch in hours, supply skyrockets. But demand still follows trust, relevance, and clear value. The median AI-built app doesn’t fail because of poor code. It fails because no one knows it exists or why it matters.
                      - text: From my perspective, this is a strategic wake-up call.
                      - text: The competitive edge is no longer technical capability alone. It’s positioning, problem clarity, user insight, and go-to-market discipline.
                      - text: AI has democratised creation. It has not democratised distribution.
                      - text: The builders who win won’t just ship faster. They’ll think harder about who they’re serving and why their solution deserves attention.
                      - text: "So here’s the real question:"
                      - text: Are you optimising for building… or for being chosen?

# bird 🐦

Fast X/Twitter CLI using GraphQL + cookie auth.

## Install

```bash
# npm/pnpm/bun
npm install -g @steipete/bird

# Homebrew (macOS, prebuilt binary)
brew install steipete/tap/bird

# One-shot (no install)
bunx @steipete/bird whoami
```

## Authentication

`bird` uses cookie-based auth.

Use `--auth-token` / `--ct0` to pass cookies directly, or `--cookie-source` for browser cookies.

Run `bird check` to see which source is active. For Arc/Brave, use `--chrome-profile-dir <path>`.

## Commands

### Account & Auth

```bash
bird whoami                    # Show logged-in account
bird check                     # Show credential sources
bird query-ids --fresh         # Refresh GraphQL query ID cache
```

### Reading Tweets

```bash
bird read <url-or-id>          # Read a single tweet
bird <url-or-id>               # Shorthand for read
bird thread <url-or-id>        # Full conversation thread
bird replies <url-or-id>       # List replies to a tweet
```

### Timelines

```bash
bird home                      # Home timeline (For You)
bird home --following          # Following timeline
bird user-tweets @handle -n 20 # User's profile timeline
bird mentions                  # Tweets mentioning you
bird mentions --user @handle   # Mentions of another user
```

### Search

```bash
bird search "query" -n 10
bird search "from:steipete" --all --max-pages 3
```

### News & Trending

```bash
bird news -n 10                # AI-curated from Explore tabs
bird news --ai-only            # Filter to AI-curated only
bird news --sports             # Sports tab
bird news --with-tweets        # Include related tweets
bird trending                  # Alias for news
```

### Lists

```bash
bird lists                     # Your lists
bird lists --member-of         # Lists you're a member of
bird list-timeline <id> -n 20  # Tweets from a list
```

### Bookmarks & Likes

```bash
bird bookmarks -n 10
bird bookmarks --folder-id <id>           # Specific folder
bird bookmarks --include-parent           # Include parent tweet
bird bookmarks --author-chain             # Author's self-reply chain
bird bookmarks --full-chain-only          # Full reply chain
bird unbookmark <url-or-id>
bird likes -n 10
```

### Social Graph

```bash
bird following -n 20           # Users you follow
bird followers -n 20           # Users following you
bird following --user <id>     # Another user's following
bird about @handle             # Account origin/location info
```

### Engagement Actions

```bash
bird follow @handle            # Follow a user
bird unfollow @handle          # Unfollow a user
```

### Posting

```bash
bird tweet "hello world"
bird reply <url-or-id> "nice thread!"
bird tweet "check this out" --media image.png --alt "description"
```

**⚠️ Posting risks**: Posting is more likely to be rate limited; if blocked, use the browser tool instead.

## Media Uploads

```bash
bird tweet "hi" --media img.png --alt "description"
bird tweet "pics" --media a.jpg --media b.jpg  # Up to 4 images
bird tweet "video" --media clip.mp4            # Or 1 video
```

## Pagination

Commands supporting pagination: `replies`, `thread`, `search`, `bookmarks`, `likes`, `list-timeline`, `following`, `followers`, `user-tweets`

```bash
bird bookmarks --all                    # Fetch all pages
bird bookmarks --max-pages 3            # Limit pages
bird bookmarks --cursor <cursor>        # Resume from cursor
bird replies <id> --all --delay 1000    # Delay between pages (ms)
```

## Output Options

```bash
--json          # JSON output
--json-full     # JSON with raw API response
--plain         # No emoji, no color (script-friendly)
--no-emoji      # Disable emoji
--no-color      # Disable ANSI colors (or set NO_COLOR=1)
--quote-depth n # Max quoted tweet depth in JSON (default: 1)
```

## Global Options

```bash
--auth-token <token>       # Set auth_token cookie
--ct0 <token>              # Set ct0 cookie
--cookie-source <source>   # Cookie source for browser cookies (repeatable)
--chrome-profile <name>    # Chrome profile name
--chrome-profile-dir <path> # Chrome/Chromium profile dir or cookie DB path
--firefox-profile <name>   # Firefox profile
--timeout <ms>             # Request timeout
--cookie-timeout <ms>      # Cookie extraction timeout
```

## Config File

`~/.config/bird/config.json5` (global) or `./.birdrc.json5` (project):

```json5
{
  cookieSource: ["chrome"],
  chromeProfileDir: "/path/to/Arc/Profile",
  timeoutMs: 20000,
  quoteDepth: 1,
}
```

Environment variables: `BIRD_TIMEOUT_MS`, `BIRD_COOKIE_TIMEOUT_MS`, `BIRD_QUOTE_DEPTH`

## Troubleshooting

### Query IDs stale (404 errors)

```bash
bird query-ids --fresh
```

### Cookie extraction fails

- Check browser is logged into X
- Try different `--cookie-source`
- For Arc/Brave: use `--chrome-profile-dir`

---

**TL;DR**: Read/search/engage with CLI. Post carefully or use browser. 🐦
